definition: length-dependent isometric bound: per coordinate, the sum over muscles whose moment arm points the same way as the demand of max isometric force times the active force-length multiplier and the cosine of the pennation angle at the posed state; no tendon compliance, passive force, activation dynamics or simultaneous multi-joint coupling
sourceOfDemand: replayed inverse dynamics in .cache and the published N m/kg CSV scaled by the subject-mass table, as in audit_bilateral_joint_capacity.py

limits: capacity is a model property, not a measurement of this or any person
the model was scaled geometrically; maximum isometric forces were not individualised

the 54-muscle model reduces the muscle set (see its own credits) so its single vas_int stands in for the vasti group; the 92-muscle comparison in docs/data/gait2392_deep_squat_capacity_AB01.json shows that stand-in is not weaker
a demand above the bound means this model cannot produce the moment; it does not prove the experimental moment is wrong or that a real person could not perform the lift

the experimental knee demand differs by a large factor between the two subjects and between the two legs of one subject, so that axis cannot be read as a person's capacity shortfall without first explaining the demand
the hamstring knee moment arm changes sign beyond about 125 deg of flexion in this model, so part of the knee bound comes from muscles acting there as knee extensors
